pairs.question: Cum pateris sapiens emendatusque uocari, respondesne tuo, dic sodes, nomine?
pairs.answer: Nempe uir bonus et prudens dici delector ego ac tu.
pairs.derivation: Horace's interrogative respondesne...nomine? (-ne enclitic), with the cum-clause kept as verbatim setup so 'answering to your name' is intelligible. The parenthetical dic sodes is the author's own contiguous words, kept rather than excised mid-sentence. The interlocutor's quoted reply 'Nempe uir bonus...ac tu.' is the answer; it ends at the full stop, after which the text turns to Qui dedit hoc hodie (a new thought about Fortune), so the answer stops there.

pairs.question: Vir bonus est quis?
pairs.answer: Qui consulta patrum, qui leges iuraque seruat, quo multae magnaeque secantur iudice lites, quo res sponsore et quo causae teste tenentur.
pairs.derivation: Horace poses the interrogative Vir bonus est quis? (quis) and supplies a quoted definition as the answer. Answer runs to the full stop ending tenentur; the following Sed uidet hunc omnis domus (the rejoinder undercutting that definition) is a new movement, so the answer stops at tenentur.

pairs.question: Pentheu, rector Thebarum, quid me perferre patique indignum coges?
pairs.derivation: The vir bonus (in the role of Bacchus) asks Pentheus the interrogative quid...coges?; the vocative Pentheu, rector Thebarum is part of his utterance and kept, while the speech tag Vir bonus et sapiens audebit dicere: is dropped as framing. Pentheus' reply 'Adimam bona.' directly answers; the window stops at that full stop, before the speaker's further retort 'Nempe pecus, rem...' begins.
